analysis.title: Global Economic Weekly: Shaken and stirred
key_insights: Equities are selling off alongside Middle East tensions and AI-trade concerns. BofA argues the debt-issuance explanation does not fit, because long-end US rates are rallying (10y back below 5%) while equities fall. It reads this as the market questioning whether tech firms can monetize AI investment.

French 10y OAT yields rose to their highest since 2002 and sit above US 10y yields for the first time since the Eurozone crisis. BofA cites social unrest and a weak outlook for fiscal consolidation ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Crude is above $110/bbl on reports of increased military operations after the US midterms. Hostilities are hitting refining capacity and pressuring diesel and other refined products. BofA sees no near-term de-escalation trigger and no material energy relief for inflation into next year.

BofA keeps its call for a 25bp Fed hike in October, but acknowledges it would be a heavy lift given this week's price action. Only 2bp is priced for next week, and markets price about a 10% chance of an October hike. BofA has high conviction the Fed should hike but low conviction that it will.
The large, broad-based beat in September inflation offset last month's downward revisions. Core PCE could plausibly end 2026 at 3.4% y/y, assuming September core PCE of 0.35% m/m.
The 10y yield has nearly fallen back below 5% and the 10y term premium is down over 25bp. This undercuts the argument that long-end yields are doing the Fed's tightening work.

The October FOMC tests Chair Warsh's resolve to bring a 'sea change' to forward guidance. Williams and Jefferson's guidance led markets to price out the October hike. BofA says a hike would signal the Fed has exited coordinated messaging.

If the Fed hikes, the risk is a policy-error (over-tightening) trade: a large risk-asset correction with twist-flattening of the curve. If it holds, the risk is a credibility trade like the July presser: twist-steepening, a weaker dollar and a moderate risk-asset selloff.
Even if the Fed holds in October, BofA still expects hikes in December 2026 and March 2027. Risks tilt toward more hikes in June and perhaps September 2027 if y/y inflation stays sticky.

BofA expects the ECB to hold next week and lean slightly dovish, with tighter financial conditions offsetting renewed energy-price risk. It keeps a hiking bias, expects one final hike in December (some March risk if energy stays high), and sees cuts in late 2027.

BofA sees the ECB cumulative hiking cycle at 75bp, with residual risk of 100bp. It sees room for verbal intervention on long-term rates and spreads, including a possible temporary QT pause if markets stay disorderly. The bar for structurally ending QT is high.
UK September CPI rose to 3.5% from 3.1% (0.53% m/m), 10bp above consensus and 44bp above the BoE forecast. Core rose to 2.8% and services to 3.7%. Energy inflation rose to 17.9% from 13.8%.

UK labour data was stronger than expected: unemployment fell to 4.7% from 4.9%, and payroll revisions were upward. BofA reads the labour market as stabilizing. It keeps its call for BoE hikes in November and February to 4.25% and calls market pricing of close to four hikes excessive.

BofA forecasts UK headline inflation peaking at 4.2% in February 2027, and expects a low-key Autumn Budget. It sees pre-measures headroom cut by about £14bn to about £10bn, about £8bn of tax rises, and borrowing £15bn higher than March in FY26-27 at £130.5bn.

The Philippines targets a fiscal deficit of 3.5% of GDP by 2030, down from 5.6% in 2025. This relies on 5-6% GDP growth, easing oil and inflation, and new taxes. BofA says the pace may be slower, and the 2027 deficit is placed at P1.66trn (5.4% of GDP). New taxes may raise only P40-50bn a year.

SSA sentiment is constructive on improving fundamentals and commodities. Election and fiscal risks are rising in Kenya and Angola, and Senegal's debt restructuring perimeter, comparability of treatment and LIC-DSF questions remain unresolved.

In Nigeria, the CBN cut the MPR by 350bp to 23.0% and narrowed the corridor, which BofA reads as roughly 200bp of effective easing. BofA no longer expects a November cut and sees the next possible easing in February 2027 or later. South Africa's SARB could hike if inflation surprises up and the Fed hikes in October.

Central American oil-shock effects on external accounts are limited. Gold and tourism cushion the Dominican Republic, tourism helps Costa Rica, and remittances support Guatemala. BofA's commodities team forecasts Brent averaging $91 in 2026 and $80 in 2027.

sector_views.rationale: AI stocks lead the S&P 500 selloff. BofA reads falling long-end yields alongside falling equities as a market questioning AI monetization. It flags the AI trade breaking as possibly the biggest risk to the US outlook.

risk_factors: The AI trade breaking, which BofA calls possibly the biggest risk to the US outlook

A Fed policy-error trade, either over-tightening or lost inflation credibility

Downside risk to Caribbean and Central American tourism if fuel prices weigh on travel

tension_points.bull_case: The case for a hike is strong: Sep inflation beat was large and broad, core PCE could end 2026 at 3.4%, and a hike keeps the December option and signals the Fed has exited coordinated messaging.
tension_points.bear_case: A hike on a 10% market probability, six days before the midterms and amid the risk-off move, could trigger an over-tightening policy-error trade with a large correction in risk assets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Something breaking in markets, such as the AI trade, would undercut the case for further hikes.

tension_points.bull_case: The prevailing narrative is that the selloff reflects tech debt issuance to fund the investment boom.
tension_points.bear_case: Falling long-end yields alongside falling equities point to doubt about whether tech firms can monetize their investments.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A selloff led by rising long-end US yields would support the debt-supply narrative.

theme_stances.key_argument: Long-end rates rally while equities sell off, which points to concerns about profitability and monetization of AI investment rather than debt supply.
theme_stances.evidence: market pricing is telling us that concerns are building around profitability and monetization

theme_stances.key_argument: BofA sees a strong case for a hike but only low conviction the Fed will deliver it.
theme_stances.evidence: we have only low conviction that it will

theme_stances.key_argument: Hot inflation, firming underlying services pressure and a stabilizing labour market strengthen the case for an insurance hike.
theme_stances.evidence: strengthens the case for our call of an insurance hike in November
